questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left part of the lane, next to the centerline.
The right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It depends on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the position that gives you the best visibility and the most space around you. Move your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet?

options.text: Motorcycle riders who have had their license for less than two years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle riders under age 18.
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, all riders and passengers under age 18 must wear helmets. All riders should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: During the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times, even during daylight.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left.
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on the left, ride in the left part of your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If your rear brake locks on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop. A locked rear wheel will not cause problems as long as the motorcycle stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: How should you position your body on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not support your body. Your elbows should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Who must use eye protection?

options.text: Only riders who have had their license for less than two years.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders.
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, all motorcycle riders must use eye protection such as glasses, goggles, a face shield, or a windshield. A face shield offers the best protection.

questions.question: Where should less experienced riders be positioned in a group?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves toward the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: How should a parked motorcycle be positioned relative to the curb?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
Without any wheel or fender touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: Park a motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Where should you ride when passing parked cars?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from car doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out of spaces. Always be ready to change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights at a railroad crossing are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you move. Never try to cross in front of a train.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help a helmet protect you?

options.text: It has no cracks or damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A helmet works best when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely, then proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and pass it.
Park and wait for the dog to go away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and pass it.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, downshift and slow down. Let it approach, then accelerate away quickly.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, how should you do it?

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to both swerve and brake, do them separately. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and other vehicles.
Decrease the distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid collisions. Use the headlights of vehicles in front of you to see the road ahead. Be ready to adjust your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to watch for surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes looking ahead.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes looking ahead.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes forward when riding through a work zone. Go slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: White lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction. What do solid white lines mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. When is this strip safe to ride on?

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually gives good traction for riding, except when it rains. The strip is about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps you. Which is NOT a benefit?

options.text: You have more time to react to the movements of other drivers.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space helps you react faster to other drivers and gives you room to move safely. This means you have MORE escape routes, not fewer.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, where should you secure it?
questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads as low as possible to protect your motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: A vehicle is passing you on the left. Where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on the left. Riding on the right may encourage the other driver to return to your lane too quickly, which is dangerous.
